subject: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier
item: divergence 1 (fails_wrongly) at t=0 ms: The road user's velocity [-2.4, 14.3] has magnitude 14.5 m/s and absolute cosine exactly 0.6 with carrier direction [20, 21], meeting the inclusive threshold. Micrometre truncation in the direction reader slightly enlarges the normalised vector, causing the body to reject this boundary case. — contract: holds, body: fails; contract: "a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction (st.lane_direction) an angle whose cosine, in absolute value, is at most cos_max"
reason: The contract states its test as a dot product with "the normalised direction", and the atom contract for st.lane_direction defines that reading: the vector is the unit vector times a factor of at least 1, exactly the unit vector only where the scaled length is a whole number of micrometres. For [20, 21] that length is 29/21, which is not a whole number of micrometres, so the read vector is slightly longer than the unit vector. Under that disclosed reading, the dot product at this exact boundary (8.7 against 0.6 × 14.5) slightly exceeds cos_max times the speed, which gives the body's verdict. — "the absolute value of the dot product of the velocity with the normalised direction is at most cos_max times the speed"
situation: The road user's velocity [-2.4, 14.3] has magnitude 14.5 m/s and absolute cosine exactly 0.6 with carrier direction [20, 21], meeting the inclusive threshold. Micrometre truncation in the direction reader slightly enlarges the normalised vector, causing the body to reject this boundary case.
contract_words: a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction (st.lane_direction) an angle whose cosine, in absolute value, is at most cos_max

subject: drv.motion.left_turn
item: divergence 1 (holds_wrongly) at t=6000 ms: A continuous leftward turn is already under way at t=0 and is still under way at t=4000 ms; the first stopped observation is t=6000 ms. The act began before the four-second window behind that observation, but the body recognizes the in-band remainder of the turn. — contract: fails, body: holds; contract: "The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized."
reason: The contract says conduct before the window is not read, and states the recognition condition in terms of the window alone. In the executed facts that condition holds at t=6000 ms and did not hold at t=4000 ms: yaw rate 30 deg/s at 2000 and 4000 ms gives an in-band heading change, then yaw rate 0 at 6000 ms. A reasonable reading therefore treats the recognized act as the turning within the window, so it begins there, and gives the body's verdict. — "Conduct before the window behind is not read"
situation: A continuous leftward turn is already under way at t=0 and is still under way at t=4000 ms; the first stopped observation is t=6000 ms. The act began before the four-second window behind that observation, but the body recognizes the in-band remainder of the turn.
contract_words: The act begins within the window behind the observation at which it is recognized.
